references.text: In [ref:Luk 19:26|Luke 19:26], Jesus gives the overarching principle that explains the command in verse 24: "I tell you, to everyone who has, more will be given, and from the one who does not have, even what they have will be taken away." This is the reason why the mina was taken from the lazy servant and given to the one who had ten.

In Jesus' parable of the talents in [ref:Matt 25:28-29|Matthew 25:28-29], an almost identical command is given: the talent is taken from the useless servant and given to the one who has ten talents, followed by the same principle that whoever has will be given more. This is a parallel parable with the same point.

[ref:Matt 13:12|Matthew 13:12] expresses the same principle in another context: "For to everyone who has, more will be given, and they will have an abundance. But from the one who does not have, even what they have will be taken away." This supports the spiritual principle behind the command in Luke 19:24.

[ref:Mark 4:25|Mark 4:25] repeats the same principle in connection with Jesus' teaching on hearing and receiving: "For to everyone who has, more will be given. And from the one who does not have, even what they have will be taken away."

In [ref:Luk 16:10-12|Luke 16:10-12], Jesus speaks about faithfulness in small things as a prerequisite for being entrusted with more. The servant who managed his mina well was rewarded with more, while the unfaithful servant lost what he had. The principle of faithful stewardship is repeated.

[ref:Luk 19:16-17|Luke 19:16-17] tells about the servant who earned ten minas and is rewarded with authority over ten cities. It is to this faithful servant that the mina from the lazy servant is transferred, emphasizing that faithful stewardship is further rewarded.
